summary:
I've been working on a few things at once, and the most interesting one is the integration between The Long Rest, a campaign manager for tabletop D&D, and Foundry. I wrote a Foundry module that pulls a session's NPCs, reveals and rolls out of the app, then published it through a script that builds one squashed, leak-scanned commit per release. The hard part was testing it. Foundry strips undefined fields from the objects you hand it on create, so my own reveal keys vanished mid-import. For a while I thought a call had hung. It turned out to be a one-minute error back-off.

Around that I've been tightening the app's privacy rules. Players only see NPC text that has passed through a single redaction layer, and the Oracle's search index follows the same rules. I also found that the campaign endpoint was sending every member the full campaign and member rows, which included encrypted provider tokens and everyone's email. It now returns only the fields each role is supposed to see. I checked the fix on the live site with two real accounts.

I added a way to import a published adventure by pasting it in. The model derives Codex, bestiary and prep-tome proposals, the DM reviews them, and the source text is deleted once they're applied. Photo import came next. It runs into a content filter that refuses to transcribe copyrighted prose. It handles tables and stat blocks fine, so I scoped it to those. Haiku also got numbers wrong in photographed tables without flagging them, so transcription runs on a bigger model.

On the home side, the GPU that runs my local models was loud even when idle. Two fan controllers were fighting over the same channel. The loud part was the card sitting warm with a model loaded, not the card being busy. I also built a hallway light that turns red during meetings, so my family knows when I'm on a call.

highlights.oneLiner: Foundry module pulls a session's NPCs, reveals and rolls out of the app.
Tracked a loud idle GPU to two fan controllers fighting over one channel.
Tightening redaction so players only see NPC text that passed one layer.
